Actually positions: 1 = W three-hand; 2-3 series "BP" = Aquaracer Professional; 4 = movement type 1 quartz/2 automatic; here 4th char is "2" → automatic ✓ (WBP201A). Then 5 = size class, 6 = metal, 7 = dial version.

WBP201A: 4th char = 2 (automatic), 5th = 0, 6th = 1 (steel), 7th = A (dial version, letter). Hmm, so the format is W-BP-2-0-1-A: pos1 W, pos2-3 BP, pos4 2, pos5 0, pos6 1 (metal steel), pos7 A.

So for a black DLC version, metal digit would be different — maybe 2? Hmm. TAG Heuer Aquaracer Professional 300 DLC references: WBP201D? That doesn't fit the 7-character pattern W BP 2 0 1 D... Actually the 7th position is dial version, which can be a letter. So WBP201D: pos6=1 (steel) hmm but the case is DLC steel which is still steel base.

Actually I recall the Aquaracer Professional 300 black DLC with white dial: WBP201D.FT6197. Hmm, but wait — the metal digit 1 = steel, and DLC-coated steel is still steel. And the dial would be... "D" hmm.

Yes! I'm fairly confident: TAG Heuer Aquaracer Professional 300 — WBP201A (black), WBP201B (blue), WBP201C (green?), WBP201D (silver/white opaline dial). And the DLC version would be... hmm, actually the black DLC case.

Hmm wait, there's also the "Aquaracer Professional 300 Night Diver" WBP2010.FT6197 — full black DLC (titanium? no, steel DLC) with black dial. So the pos5 might be size class, pos6 metal. WBP2010: pos5=0? Hmm WBP2010 = W BP 2 0 1 0 → the 7th char is "0"? That breaks the pattern of 7 chars.

Actually WBP2010 has 7 chars: W,B,P,2,0,1,0. Hmm. And WBP201A is W,B,P,2,0,1,A. So pos7 is the dial/version code, which can be a letter or digit.
